chapter: Woody Herman, Henderson and the Indiana Theater
title: A William Tell arrangement for Duke Ellington
summary: He wrote a special William Tell for Duke Ellington, who said he would play it, but Ben Webster told him it never got done.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Yeah. You did some writing for Duke Ellington, too, didn't you?
Yes, I did. I did that -- Duke told me, if it's the last thing he do, he's going to play that William Tell. I did a special arrangement for Duke on William Tell.
Same type of arrangement that you had for the WPA band?

Only one thing, I think I kind of escalated it a little more. Instead of de-escalating the work in it, I kind of loosened it up a little more, and maybe that's what messed it up. Because the late Ben Webster, when -- one day, on 39th Street. I said, Ben, what did he do about that arrangement, because Duke said he was going to rehearse it when he got to California? I said, what did you do about it? Because I don't think the arrangements is all that hard. He say, What? I said, I don't think the arrangement's all that hard. But Duke told me, if it's the last thing he's going to do, he's going to play it. But I never did hear him play it.
